name: Turkmenistan
summary: A green field with a vertical red band at the hoist bearing five ornate carpet guls above crossed olive branches, and a white crescent with five stars in the upper hoist of the green. It is often described as the most intricate national flag.
origin: Turkmenistan adopted its first post-Soviet flag on 19 February 1992. The olive branches were added in 1997, symbolising the country's neutrality, recognised by the UN General Assembly in 1995.
In 2001 the proportions were changed from 1:2 to 2:3. The design reflects President Saparmurat Niyazov's emphasis on Turkmen identity and traditional carpets.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Islam and the traditional Turkmen colour.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The background of the carpet band.

symbols.name: Five carpet guls
symbols.description: Stacked medallions from traditional Turkmen carpets, in the red band.
symbols.meaning: The five major Turkmen tribes: Teke, Yomut, Arsary, Chowdur and Saryk.

symbols.name: Olive branches
symbols.description: Crossed olive branches beneath the guls.

symbols.name: Crescent and five stars
symbols.description: A white crescent with five stars.
symbols.meaning: Hope for a bright future; the stars stand for the five provinces (welayats).

facts: The carpet guls are among the most detailed designs on any national flag.
Flag and Constitution Day is celebrated on 18 May.
Turkmenistan's neutrality is commemorated by the Arch of Neutrality in Ashgabat.
clues: Green with a red hoist band of carpet patterns, olive branches, and a white crescent with five stars.
Its band shows designs from five tribes' carpets.
Olive branches were added for its UN-recognised neutrality.
